summary: Create a reversed view without changing the source array.
documentation: toReversed returns a new array with elements in the opposite order. Unlike reverse, it leaves the receiver’s order intact. The copy is shallow: nested objects remain the same objects.
returns: A new array in reverse order.
caution: Reversing a sequence does not sort it. A copied array still shares references to its nested objects.
scenarios: Display a newest-first history while retaining chronological source data.
Show undo actions starting with the latest recorded change.
title: Show both history directions
problem: Input is an array of event labels in chronological order. Return {chronological: inputOrder, newestFirst: reversedOrder}. Preserve duplicates and leave the chronological order intact.
goal: Use Array.toReversed() or an equivalent approach demonstrating the same premise.
hint: Build a reversed copy, rather than reversing the shared source array.
